seoTitle: Free JSON to Go Struct Generator Online
metaDescription: Free online JSON to Go struct generator. Create Go structs with json tags from a sample, with idiomatic names like ID and URL. Runs in your browser.
intro: Generate Go struct definitions with json tags from a JSON sample. Field names are converted to exported Go names, and fields missing in some items get omitempty.
why:
Decoding JSON in Go needs a struct that matches the data, with exported field names and json tags. Writing one for a large response means a lot of typing and easy mistakes, such as a lowercase field that never gets filled or a tag that does not match the key.

Paste a sample response and the tool produces nested structs, turns snake_case keys into names like UserName, and uses common initialisms such as ID, URL and HTTP. Integers become int64 and other numbers float64. A field that is null in the sample, or absent in some array items, becomes a pointer or gets omitempty. Review the result, since a sample cannot show every variation. Nothing is uploaded; it runs in your browser.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample into the input box.
Set the root struct name, for example Response or User.
Copy the generated structs into your Go file.
Adjust types by hand where the sample is not representative.

faq.a: Keys are split into words and converted to exported Go names, so user_name becomes UserName. Common initialisms such as ID, URL, API and HTTP are written in capitals. The original key stays in the json tag.
Strings become string, booleans bool, whole numbers int64 and other numbers float64. Objects become named structs and arrays become slices. Mixed or unknown values fall back to interface{}.

faq.q: What does a null value become?
faq.a: If a field is null in one place and a value elsewhere, it becomes a pointer, such as *string. A field that is only null, or empty arrays, become interface{} because the type cannot be known.
Yes, for keys that are missing from some items when array elements are merged. Fields present everywhere get a plain json tag.
